Plot an hv_mirror_hist object

Source: R/mirror-histogram.R
plot.hv_mirror_hist.Rd

Builds a bare mirrored-histogram ggplot2 object from an hv_mirror_hist data object. Bars for the treated group appear above the x-axis; bars for the control group appear below. Matched or weighted patients are shown in a contrasting shade. Compose with + to add color scales, axis labels, and theme_hv_manuscript.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'hv_mirror_hist'
plot(x, alpha = 0.8, split_tall = FALSE, split_mult = 1.5, ...)

Arguments

x

An hv_mirror_hist object from hv_mirror_hist. The fill legend reads "<group>, all" and "<group>, matched" (or ", weighted") from group_labels. A scale_fill_manual() you add replaces that scale; pass labels = x$meta$fill_labels to keep the readable labels.

When one arm piles into a single bin (say 648 of 685 patients at a score of 95 to 100\ arm and the matched bars cannot be read. split_tall = TRUE sizes the y-axis to the tallest bar of the matched (or weighted) layers or of the arm whose tallest bar is smaller, times split_mult. Any taller "all patients" bar is clipped at the panel edge, cut by a white gap, and labeled with its full count on a white label. The limits are set with coord_cartesian, which clips a bar instead of dropping it, so do not add ylim() or scale limits on top; a scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) without limits is safe.

alpha

Bar transparency in \([0,1]\). Default 0.8.

split_tall

Logical. Split "all patients" bars too tall for an axis sized to the matched bars and the smaller arm. Default FALSE.

split_mult

Number greater than 1: the axis cap as a multiple of the tallest matched bar or tallest bar of the smaller arm. Used only when split_tall = TRUE. Default 1.5.

...

Ignored; present for S3 consistency.

Value

A bare ggplot object; compose with + to add color scales, axis limits, labels, and theme_hv_manuscript. With split_tall = TRUE it carries two extra layers after the bars: the white gaps (geom_rect) and the count labels (geom_label).

See also

hv_mirror_hist to build the data object, theme_hv_manuscript for the publication theme, sample_mirror_histogram_data for example data.

Other Propensity Score & Matching: hv_mirror_hist(), hv_rmst_contrast(), hv_rmst_curves(), plot.hv_rmst_contrast(), plot.hv_rmst_curves(), sample_covariate_balance_data()

Examples

dta <- sample_mirror_histogram_data(n = 500)
mh  <- hv_mirror_hist(dta)
#> mirror_histogram diagnostics: n=1000  dropped=0  [see $tables$diagnostics]

plot(mh) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Propensity Score (%)", y = "Count") +
  theme_hv_poster()


# One tall bar: most treated patients pile into the top bin.
dta_tall <- dta
top <- dta_tall$tavr == 1 & dta_tall$match == 0
dta_tall$prob_t[top] <- 0.98
mh_tall <- hv_mirror_hist(dta_tall)
#> mirror_histogram diagnostics: n=1000  dropped=0  [see $tables$diagnostics]
plot(mh_tall, split_tall = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Propensity Score (%)", y = "Count") +
  theme_hv_poster()
